name: Tactile: Giving Computer-Using Agents Hands and Feet

name: Qwen-UI-Agent Technical Report: Toward Next-Generation Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Describes a foundation GUI agent with combined GUI and command-line actions, large-scale interaction infrastructure, and iterative environment and task generation.

name: Screenshots or Tools? Eliciting Tool Use and Managing Multimodal Context in Hybrid GUI-MCP Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: WebRider: Persona-Conditioned Intent Controllers for Live-Web Assistance
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). RiderBench evaluates live-web contracts across 42 public websites.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: MCP-Driven Accessibility Tree Standardization for AI-Powered Screen Reader Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: AutoTailor: Automatic, User-Aligned Capability Selection and Adaptation for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: RecreationWorld: Scalable and Verifiable Environments for Hybrid Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: MintAct: A Unified Visual Agent for Digital Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: agent-computer-use
notes: Published on npm as agent-cu (package.json 0.1.1 at the inspected commit) with precompiled binaries, and also installable as an agent skill (skills/agent-computer-use/SKILL.md). Commands snapshot an app's accessibility tree into @eN refs or query it with a selector DSL (role, name, id, parent-child chains), then click, type, press keys, scroll, drag, move or resize windows, wait for elements, take screenshots, and run JSON batches or YAML workflows; output is JSON by default. Backends: macOS uses AXUIElement with CGEvent input, Windows uses UI Automation, and Linux uses AT-SPI2 over D-Bus with xdotool for input. Electron apps can be driven over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, but automatic Electron detection and relaunch with a debug port is implemented only on macOS (cli/crates/agent-computer-use-cdp/src/detect.rs). The README marks every platform as preview and states that the project is no longer maintained, recommending Cua Driver instead. The repository was formerly named kortix-ai/agent-click (same GitHub repository ID). The tool contains no model or agent loop.

notes: Electron app (desktop/) that starts a local Next.js server (app/, lib/server/) on port 3210; version 0.0.28 in package.json, matching release tag v0.0.28 at 92ec73d, and the inspected commit 62c7f98 is later. Bots' tasks run on Orgo cloud computers launched from the bops-base template that orgo/bops-base.mjs builds from vm/ (Codex, the screen MCP and per-screen Chrome helpers). By default lib/server/computer-task.ts runs each thread on OpenAI's Responses API computer tool: Orgo's API returns a screenshot of the bot's screen, and every click, double-click, drag, scroll, typing or key press the model asks for is executed as xdotool commands through Orgo's bash endpoint, with the result screen sent back; the same loop offers a page_script tool that runs a short Playwright script on the screen's Chrome over CDP, a Linux shell, web search, a password vault and app, data and CRM tools. With BOPS_COMPUTER_TOOL=0 threads use OpenAI's Agents API with Codex and vm/screen_mcp.py, which exposes one screen's screenshot and input actions over MCP. Tasks on the user's own Mac run in a bot-owned Chrome; with Full access they also get a shell and the user's apps through Cua Driver behind vm/mac-ui-mcp.mjs, which hides sensitive apps, sends input only in the background and blocks quitting, copying and pasting (lib/server/local.ts). Per the README, reading runs at once while sending, creating and paying wait for the user's approval, and any screen can be watched live and taken over. Self-hosting requires an Orgo account and two OpenAI API keys, with Honcho, Composio, treg, AgentMail, AgentPhone and TypeSafe recommended or optional; signing in with Orgo instead routes provider calls through Orgo's hosted Bops Cloud (cloud/). name: Xiryn
notes: Next.js app run locally (version 0.4.1 in package.json; tag v0.4.1 points at b8016b5, and the inspected commit 489e9c4 is later). Each agent's workstation is a Docker container built from workstation/: Debian (trixie-slim) with Xvfb, xfwm4 and a panel, Chromium, x11vnc and noVNC, xdotool and scrot, a persistent home volume, and an inactivity watchdog. lib/agent/tools.ts defines the tool belt for the Vercel AI SDK streamText loop: shell and fs_* through docker exec; screen_capture and screen_share (scrot JPEG through xiryn-shot); pointer_click, pointer_move, pointer_drag, pointer_scroll, key_type and key_press (xdotool in lib/workstation.ts), each returning a fresh screenshot; request_takeover; vault_list, vault_fill, request_payment_approval and request_secret; memory_write and memory_forget; web_search and web_fetch through Firecrawl; and delegate for squads. Observation is plain screenshots of a 1280x800 display with pixel coordinates; there is no accessibility tree or element annotation. Before each step the runtime keeps only the two most recent screenshots in full (docs/architecture.md). The vault fills saved logins and cards into fields without the model seeing them, and cards only after the owner approves the payment. The user can watch and take over the desktop, and the agent hands over at logins, payments, one-time codes or CAPTCHAs, with a Telegram notice when paired. Models come from the owner's keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The README's comparison with hosted agents is the author's own. Root LICENSE is MIT.

name: Computer Agent Arena: Toward Human-Centric Evaluation and Analysis of Computer-Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the ICLR 2026 proceedings page and abstract, the full proceedings PDF and the platform README at commit 4536036; the OpenReview forum lists it as an ICLR 2026 Poster. Two anonymized agents run the same user-written instruction in parallel, identically initialized Ubuntu or Windows virtual machines on AWS EC2, shown to users through a browser VNC view and synchronized replays; the paper turns the pairwise votes into a Bradley-Terry ranking and also collects optional step-level labels. It reports 2,201 filtered votes from 1,058 users over 12 agents, compares pure GUI agents with agents that also call tools or write code, and links github.com/xlang-ai/computer-agent-arena for the platform and a Hugging Face page for the collected data; neither release was reviewed here. No arXiv version was found.
summary: Crowdsourced arena where users set tasks on cloud Ubuntu or Windows desktops, watch two anonymous computer-use agents attempt them side by side and vote; reports 2,201 votes over 12 agents.

name: Komos
notes: The documentation describes a task as a reusable automation graph. Its Agent Action node handles browser steps (navigating, clicking, filling forms, scrolling, extracting) from a natural-language prompt, can also call integrations and inspect captured network requests, and accepts screenshots as visual references. A task can be trained from a narrated screen or tab recording of up to five minutes, which Komos turns into a plan, or built step by step in a visual builder. Runs use a fresh or persistent cloud Chromium sandbox on Daytona compute, or a self-hosted runner on a Windows or macOS host that can reuse SSO sessions; the Chrome extension path is retired. The built-in assistant Moss creates, schedules and debugs tasks from chat and is also reachable from coding agents through an MCP server. The agent's model is unspecified.
summary: Hosted automation platform whose task flows use a prompt-driven agent to navigate, click, type and extract on websites in a cloud Chromium sandbox or self-hosted runner, built from narrated screen recordings or chat.

name: Gumloop
notes: Recorded as adjacent: Gumloop presents itself as a platform for building, sharing and running AI agents for business teams, which work mainly through app connectors, MCP servers and APIs, and its help pages advise using the agent browser only when no connector or API covers a task. The agent browser is an ability turned on per custom agent, and on Enterprise organizations it is off by default until an admin adds it to a role. It runs Chromium on the agent's computer, which shares the agent's code sandbox, and opens pages, clicks, types, scrolls and switches tabs. Gumloop types saved logins and 2FA codes for the agent without showing them to the model, keeps sign-ins in browser profiles, offers residential proxies and desktop or Pixel 7 mobile emulation, and pauses to hand the live browser to a person at logins, CAPTCHAs or purchase confirmations. Every browser step is recorded for replay. Agents can also be reached from Slack, Microsoft Teams, email and text messages.
summary: Business agent platform whose agents work through app connectors and can turn on a Chromium browser that clicks, types, signs in with saved logins and hands control to a person when a site needs it.

name: Yutori
notes: Yutori was founded by Abhishek Das, Devi Parikh and Dhruv Batra and announced its seed round in March 2025. Navigator models are called through an OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible endpoint: the caller sends a screenshot and a task, the model returns actions as tool calls, and the caller executes them and sends a fresh screenshot in an agent loop. n1.5 drives browsers in a normalized 1000x1000 coordinate space with a core set of 18 coordinate-based tools or an expanded set that adds element extraction, find, set_element_value and JavaScript execution, and can return JSON matching a caller schema. n2 operates a full desktop through batched GUI actions plus bash and file tools; the SDK ships local Docker and Daytona examples, and Yutori MCP runs it on the visible macOS desktop, sending screen contents to Yutori. A Python SDK wraps the APIs, a CLI runs research, browsing and Scout tasks, and an MCP server with workflow skills exposes these tasks and computer use to coding agents. Scouts monitor the web on a schedule, and Delegate is a consumer agent meant to complete handed-off tasks independently. Yutori also publishes a computer-use leaderboards page compiling reported results for six benchmarks. The publisher describes its Online-Mind2Web figure as independently verified and its Navi-Bench v2 and Westworld figures as its own evaluations.
summary: Yutori's web-agent platform: the Navigator computer-use model API (n1.5 for browsers, n2 for full desktops), task APIs for browsing, research and Scout web monitoring, and the Delegate personal agent.
